blocks.heading: Checkpoint Audit and Temporal Constraints
blocks.text: The available audit snapshots record the direction-selection state for the mechanism-replacement route without asserting a temporal iteration order. Because no auditable timestamp, parent identifier, or diff is supplied, these snapshots are treated as parallel provenance records rather than a developmental sequence. This constraint prevents the appendix from converting idea history into evidence for the formal argument. The route therefore centers on the retained scope correction: pointwise energy-condition assumptions are replaced by an averaged null condition plus an independent averaged-focusing premise, while the observed stellar mass gap is demoted to an astrophysical consistency constraint.

blocks.heading: Checkpoint-to-Argument Decisions
blocks.text:
| Decision | Retained scope | Consequence for the proposal |
|---|---|---|
| Energy-condition relaxation | Use averaged null positivity only where a separate integrated focusing premise is declared | Prevents AANEC from being silently promoted into a pointwise focusing theorem |
| Mass-gap interpretation | Treat the 2-5 solar-mass interval as a consistency check, not a theorem-derived prediction | Keeps formal GR claims separate from explosion, fallback, equation-of-state, rotation, magnetic-field, nonspherical, and binary-evolution explanations |

blocks.heading: Source-Grounded Scope Corrections
blocks.text: The checkpoint audit preserves the upstream correction that quantum stress-energy can violate pointwise energy conditions while still supporting weaker averaged or inequality-based bounds (W3009127927). This motivates the retained AANEC-plus-averaged-focusing structure, but it also fixes the proof obligation: the added focusing premise must be stated independently of AANEC and must be checked against candidate witnesses rather than inferred from the energy condition. The survey material likewise identifies trapped-surface formation as the fragile boundary condition in classical singularity arguments, which is why the route's counterexample search is centered on stable ultra-compact configurations rather than on observational mass-gap demographics alone.

blocks.heading: Astrophysical Boundary Preserved by the Audit
blocks.text: The audit snapshots retain the separation between the formal theorem class and astrophysical inference. Stellar-mass measurements and population inferences (W4226083230) remain relevant only as external consistency checks; they do not validate the theorem's assumptions or its conclusion. The same applies to compact-object observations that challenge simple formation channels (W3036761016) and to equation-of-state or radius constraints that depend on additional physical assumptions (W2807309204). These sources strengthen the argument's boundary discipline: they show why the mass gap cannot be read as a direct consequence of a trapped-surface bound, and why alternative explanations must remain explicitly admissible in the proposal.

blocks.heading: Transition to the Forward Derivation
blocks.text: The next stage should therefore begin from the checkpoint-audited premises: classical spherical collapse, AANEC, global hyperbolicity, complete null generators, and an explicit integrated focusing hypothesis whose mathematical form remains to be fixed by the definition ledger. The forward derivation must then test whether the proposed Raychaudhuri-type focusing chain can support a compactness threshold without smuggling in pointwise assumptions. Candidate counterexamples are useful only if they satisfy every declared premise, including the independent focusing condition and the stability predicate; otherwise they are boundary diagnostics rather than falsifiers.
